CORAM: NEERAJ P. DHOTE, J.
DATED : 26.03.2026.
ORAL JUDGMENT

This is an Appeal under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short "L.A. Act") by the Acquiring Body against the judgment and award dated 19.12.2020 passed by the learned Joint Civil Judge, Senior Division, Nagpur (Reference Court) in Reference No.198/2002.

The operative of the same reads as under:-
"i) The application is partly allowed with proportionate costs.
ii) The non-applicants shall pay compensation Rs.
1,11,40,000/-in total for the land, fruit bearing trees and teak wood trees to the applicant.
iii) The non-applicants shall also pay 30% solatium to the applicant.
iv) The non-applicants shall also pay the additional component compensation @ 12% per annum from the date of Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act till the date of passing the award i.e. 06.07.2000 under Section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act to the applicant.
v) Whatever compensation amount already paid by the non-applicant to the applicants shall be deducted from the above said amount.
vi) The non-applicants shall pay the interest on the aforesaid enhanced amount @ 9% per annum form the date of award i.e. 06.07.2000 for the period of one year 3 fa750.2015.odt and 15% per annum for the subsequent years till its realization to the applicant.
vii) Rest of the claim of the applicant in respect of well, bunds, trees (forest) is rejected.
 viii) Decree be drawn up accordingly.
 ix) Reference application is thus, disposed of.
Judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court."

sentences.text: 2. The Respondent Nos.1 to 4 are the legal heirs of original Claimant Gulabdeo.

The land of the original Claimant admeasuring 3.20 Hectare out of Survey No.244/1 at Mouja Mendki, P.H. No.20,
Taluka Katol, District Nagpur came to be acquired for the Chikhali Nala Jalashay Prakalp.
The Section 4 notification was published on 21.03.1998 and the award was passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer (for short "S.L.A.O.") on 17.06.2000.
The S.L.A.O. determined the rate for the land at Rs.55,500/- per Hectare and awarded compensation of Rs.35,555/- towards well.
The S.L.A.O. determined the compensation towards the trees at Rs.11,92,761/-.
Being not satisfied with the compensation determined by the S.L.A.O., the original Claimant preferred Reference Application under Section 18 of the L.A. Act for enhanced compensation.
The Claimants led their evidence.
The S.L.A.O. examined himself as the witness.
No evidence was led by the Acquiring Body.

Considering the evidence on record, the learned Reference Court passed the impugned judgment and award.
4 fa750.2015.odt 3.
It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Acquiring Body that, the learned Reference Court has enhanced compensation for 400 teak trees despite there being no material on record.
He submits that, there was variance in the number of the fruit bearing trees mentioned in the Reference Application and the record.
He submits that, there is no serious challenge to the compensation enhanced for the land.
He submits that, the impugned judgment and award be appropriately modified and the Appeal be allowed.

4. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Claimants that, the enhanced compensation for the land is based on the earlier References decided by the Reference Court which were in respect of the land from the same village acquired for the same purpose, therefore, on the ground of parity the compensation at the rate of Rs.1,73,500/- per Hectare need no interference.

She submitted that, as far as the compensation for the teak trees and the fruit bearing trees is concerned, the same is based on the material available on record particularly, the Joint Measurement Report (J.M.R.).
The rate for the fruit bearing trees was determined on the basis of the earlier Reference Application which attained finality.

She submits that, since the impugned award is based on the evidence and previous decision in the Reference Application arising out of the same acquisition proceedings, no interference was called for and the Appeal be dismissed.
5. With the assistance of both the sides perused the papers on record.
There is no dispute in respect of extent of land of the Claimant acquired for the said purpose.
There is no dispute that, the 5 fa750.2015.odt acquired land belonged to the original Claimant.
The record shows that, in the J.M.R. Report at Exh.33 there is reference of 302 orange trees, 249 sweet lemon trees, 6 big trees of Yednimbu and 5 big trees of Lemon.
There is also remark showing 400 teak wood trees aged approximately 20 years.
According to the Claimants, they had raised objection to the J.M.R. Report and thereafter the entry in respect of 400 trees was made.
This aspect is not disputed by the learned Advocate for the Appellant.
The cross-examination of the S.L.A.O. goes to show that, a suggestion was given that objection was raised in respect of fruit bearing trees and teak wood trees and the same was not considered.
This being the matter of record, no fault can be found with the observations of the learned Reference Court in respect of existence of the fruit bearing trees and teak

6. The leaned Reference Court on the basis of earlier decisions in the connected Reference Applications determined the rate for the land, for the fruit bearing trees and the teak trees in paragraph Nos.15, 21, 22 to 28 of the impugned judgment which is reproduced below:-
"15) The learned counsel for the applicant also relying on the decision in L.A.C. No.
76/2001, 131/2003, 193/2003, 94/2001 and 378/2002 decided by common judgment decided on 3.5.2013 in respect of land of Mouza Mendki in which the value of the land is granted at the rate of Rs. 1,73,000/- per hector i.e. Rs. 69,400/- per acre.
21)

In view of the aforesaid decided references and the rate given by my Learned Predecessor for the vacant land and the land used for horticulture after considering the evidence of the applicant and the horticulture expert as 6 fa750.2015.odt well as the Special Land Acquisition Officer in this case, there is no impediment in accepting the rates granted it the decision relied upon by the applicant since the land is situated in the same village area with same facilities and more over the quality of the land is also similar.
22) It is to be noted here that applicants total land admeasuring 3.20 R is acquired.

Applicant is claiming compensation for 302 Orange trees, 249 Sweet Lemon Trees,
400 Teak woods trees, besides 5 - Lemon trees.

Applicant is also claiming enhancement in respect of stone bandh, mud bandh and well with pipeline.
23) While considering the facts that the orange and sweet lemon trees, land and the horticulture if approximately calculated, it is accepted that there could be 270 orange or sweet lemon trees per hector and for 550 such trees about two hectares land was admittedly under horticulture.
24) Moreover applicant is claiming compensation for 400 Teak Wood trees and these must have been existed on the remaining portion of 1 Acres of land so only one Acre land is vacant land.
Accordingly compensation has to be granted for one acre vacant land, 400 Teak Wood trees and 302 Orange Trees and 249 Mosambi Trees and 5 Lemon Trees.
25) As regards to the well, pipeline, stone and mud bandh there is absolutely no evidence except bare statement of the applicant.
Evidence of Valuer on the above subject is not adduced.
As such there is no reason to observe that the compensation granted by LAO on these subject is inadequate.
Hence applicant is not entitled for any enhancement on these subjects.

26) In view of the authority of Hon'ble Apex Court, if the sale instance is only of the land then the value of fruit trees is to be determined separately and if the sale instance includes the sale deed of land alongwith orchard and forest trees then the value of trees cannot be calculated separately as it Executive Engineer, Nagpur Medium ... vs G. sentences.text: The market value of the land, fruit bearing trees and teak wood trees as fixed in the 7 fa750.2015.odt earlier decision can be very well accepted on the ground of parity.
Non applicants have not denied or challenged the decisions in the earlier decided references.

Therefore, on the ground of parity I fixed the market price of the vacant land at the rate of Rs. 1,73,500/- per hector for the land survey No 244/1 to the extent of 1 Acre,
which comes to Rs. 69,000/- only.
Applicant is claiming at the rate of Rs. 2,00,000/- per acre which is exorbitant.

27) So far as the applicant's claim in respect of trees is concerned, applicant is entitled for compensation of Rs. 20,00,000/- for 400 Teak Wood trees @ Rs. 5000/- per teak tree, Rs.
16.61.000/- for 302 Orange trees @ Rs. 5500/- Rs. 9,96,000/- for 249 Sweet Lemon trees @ Rs.
4000/- and Rs. 5000/- for 5 Lemon trees @ Rs. 1000/- per tree. i.e. Rs. 2,26,62,000/- total of fruit trees and teak- wood trees in addition to Rs 69,000/- for one acre vacant land.
28) There is Joint Measurement Report, which is significant document for the purpose of ascertaining the existing position of the land acquired and the things attached to the land placed on record.
It shows the actual position of the land, existence of trees, room well and stone bandh."
7. The above referred observations made by the learned Reference Court goes to show that, the rate for the land, the number of trees and the rate thereof is based on the evidence available on record.
The impugned judgment by the learned Reference Court is well reasoned. Thus, no fault can be found with the same.
Resultantly, the Appeal fails.
Hence the following order:-
ORDER i) The Appeal stands dismissed with no order as to costs.
8 fa750.2015.odt ii) The balance 50% amount be deposited by the Acquiring Body within a period of

twelve (12)
weeks
. Thereafter, the Claimants shall be entitled to withdraw the same after following due process.
iii) Record and proceedings be sent back to the learned Reference Court.
(NEERAJ P. DHOTE, J.) Tambaskar.
